(AP).--An atomic device no
bigger than a can of frozen
fruit juice kept an electric light
bulb lit for 11 hours, the Los
Alamos Scientific Laboratory

tist predicted its development
would pave the way for inter-
planetary travel.

which converts atomic power
into electricity without the use
of turbines and generators, the
laboratory said.

A spokesman said the process
was several hundred times more
powerful than any used before
in converting atomic power into
electricity with the use of thermocouples.

Robert W. Pidd, the consult-
ant on the project, said the
development of the device
would pave the way for inter-
planetary travel and could
power satellites.

The device, a plasma thermo-
couple, produced enough power
to light an electric light bulb
for 11 hours before it was dis-
mantled for analysis, officials
said.

Exceeds Expectations

Mr. Pidd, professor of phys-
ics at the University of Michi-
gan, said he and other scien-
tists had expected the appara-
tus to light the bulb for only
a few minutes.

The new process is not yet
competitive with coal-made
electricity, but it is closer than
any other method, Mr. Pidd
said. Because of the lag be-
tween scientific development
and engineering, a commercial
reactor of this type is not likely
for three to 10 years, he said.

In Washington, an Atomic
Energy technician who declined
use of his name said the new
technique at its present stage
is more of an oddity than a
breakthrough. He said he be-
lieves it will have more economic
significance until it is devel-
oped further.

aimed at producing electric
power of a higher magnitude
than was the case with the pre-
viously announced atomic gen-
erator. The earlier device an-

produce power of several watts,

the objective would be to pro-
duce at least several thousand
watts.

bringing two different metals
into contact, then cooling one
metal and heating the other.

was an atomic generator de-
signed to produce power for
conventional batteries.

accomplishment.
